lead: Winston-Salem sits in the rolling North Carolina Piedmont, with red clay soil and many homes over crawl spaces. Ice storms, heavy rain and crawl space moisture drive most of its water damage.
risk: crawl space moisture, ice storm damage and heavy rain
risk_short: crawl spaces, ice storms, heavy rain
why: Many Winston-Salem homes, from the old houses of the West End and Ardmore to newer homes on the edges of town, sit over crawl spaces. Red clay soil holds water, and poor drainage keeps those spaces damp. A slow leak from a supply line or water heater can soak joists and insulation for weeks. Musty smells, soft floors and cupped hardwood are common first signs of trouble.

Ice storms are the Piedmont's big winter threat. In December 2002, a major ice storm coated the region and left most homes in the area without power, some for more than a week. Falling limbs damaged roofs, and pipes froze in cold houses. Heavy summer storms also fill Salem Creek and other streams fast, flooding low streets and yards nearby.

image_caption: Ice storms and falling limbs can open Winston-Salem roofs to leaks.
problems: Older homes in the West End, Ardmore
Crawl space drying and mold control
Wooded areas like Buena Vista, Sherwood Forest
Supply line and water heater leaks
tips: Check the crawl space after big storms and in late summer.
Add a vapor barrier and keep downspouts draining away.
Trim limbs over the roof before winter.
Insulate crawl space pipes before cold snaps.
areas: Calls come from the West End, Ardmore, Buena Vista, Old Salem, Washington Park, Sherwood Forest, Holly Avenue and Waughtown, plus Clemmons, Kernersville and Lewisville.

faq.q: Why are my Winston-Salem hardwood floors cupping?
faq.a: Cupping usually means moisture is coming from below. In many Winston-Salem homes, that is a damp crawl space or a slow plumbing leak under the floor. Fix the source first, then dry the subfloor and wood. DryFlare can measure moisture and dry the floor before it is refinished or replaced.
